JAPAN 1–2 NIGERIA | 7 NOVEMBER 2026

FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup Morocco 2026 | Final | Mohammed VI Football Complex, Rabat

Africa's First U-17 Women's World Title

Nigeria won the final on finishing and on one direct route behind Japan's line. Both teams took 12 shots; Nigeria put three on target and scored twice.

What decided the final

39'. Mary Dunstan finds Awawu Bashiru, whose dipping shot squeezes past Kou Kadowaki.

47'. Esther Stephen plays over Japan's line and Oluebube Umejiaku lobs the winner.

80'. Substitute Anri Ito heads a corner back across goal for Fuki Ito to finish.

Our verdict. Nigeria deserved the title. Japan controlled more of the ball; Nigeria created the better chances, took them, and held the lead through five minutes of stoppage time.

Phase read

What worked and where it broke down

Each point is tied to the match record or the goal footage.

Japan: the control game worked until the final third

PhaseWhat worksWhere it breaks down
In possession52.9% possession and 245 completed passes, the cleaner circulation of the two teams (63.0%).Twelve shots produced two on target and one goal (8.3% conversion).
Out of possessionThirteen tackles won and only four fouls. Disciplined, low-risk defending.A high line left space behind it. One pass from deep produced the winner at 47'.
TransitionsThe push after the 63' changes produced the corner pressure behind the 80' goal.The winner came two minutes after the restart, from a single pass.
GoalkeepingOne save, a block with the feet. Japan kept four clean sheets on the way to the final.The 39' dipping shot slipped through for the opener.
Set pieces and benchFive corners and a goal from the second ball, assisted by a 63' substitute.One goal from five corners and no goal from open play.

Nigeria: direct play won the final; pass security is the next step

PhaseWhat worksWhere it breaks down
In possessionA direct route behind the line: Stephen's pass for the 47' winner, and three offsides from the same runs.57.7% pass completion. Nigeria gave the ball back more often than Japan.
Out of possessionJapan held to two shots on target from twelve, with thirteen tackles won.Fourteen fouls. The approach worked here but carries a booking and free-kick risk against stronger set-piece sides.
TransitionsScored two minutes after half-time and hit the crossbar in the closing stages.One change all match. Japan's five substitutes brought fresher legs to the final 20 minutes.
Set piecesConceded nothing from Japan's free kicks.Japan's 80' goal came from the return ball after a corner.

Source: ESPN completed match record; FIFA and CAF match reports; broadcast review.

Tournament context

Measured against the defending champions

Japan reached the final unbeaten; Nigeria won six in a row after losing their opener. Both went through DPR Korea, the two-time holders.

Underlying record

Decisions

Five decisions from the final

Nigeria technical staffBuild the Stephen-to-Umejiaku route into the U-20 transition plan.7 Dec 2026
Nigeria defensive unitAssign second-ball marking at defensive corners.7 Dec 2026
Japan technical staffReview handling of dipping shots and cover behind the high line as two separate work items.7 Dec 2026
Both technical directorsAdd FIFA's tracking and pressing data to the match file when it publishes.6 Jan 2027
Federation leadershipFund a structured fixture calendar to keep the title-winning group together.5 Feb 2027

Japan's strongest case

More possession, more completed passes, and a late goal from the bench. The opener came from a dipping shot their goalkeeper could not hold.

Why Nigeria deserved it

More shots on target, double the conversion rate, 1.48 expected goals to 0.82, a separate well-built winner, and a late crossbar.

What this dashboard is built on

Score, scorers, assists, awards and routes come from FIFA, CAF and the national federations, matched against Graphic Online, Premium Times and Fox Sports. Team and player statistics come from ESPN's completed match record. Expected goals come from FlashFootball's live model at 89:40, before Japan's final two shots.

FIFA's post-match summary report adds tracking and pressing data; we update this dashboard when it publishes. Fox Sports' feed times the goals at 38' and 79'; FIFA and CAF record 39' and 80', which we use.
